groups.name: Elementary universe
groups.explanation: Robert Doherty (showrunner/creator), Lucy Liu (actor), Joan Watson (character), and 221B Baker Street (location) are all from the CBS series Elementary.

groups.name: Fictional small towns with a very dark secret underneath their charm
groups.explanation: Banshee (Cinemax crime drama set in a deceptively quiet PA town), Haven (Maine town plagued by supernatural 'Troubles'), Eureka (seemingly idyllic Oregon town hiding dangerous secret experiments), and Gravity Falls (Oregon tourist town concealing a world of paranormal mystery) are all fictional small towns whose quaint exteriors hide a dangerous, dark, or supernatural secret.

groups.name: Characters who leave their show permanently in a season finale — not a series finale
groups.explanation: Cristina Yang (Grey's Anatomy, exits in season 10 finale), Tara Knowles (Sons of Anarchy, killed in season 5 finale), Sansa Stark (Game of Thrones — leaves King's Landing at a season's end as a pivotal permanent departure), and Meadow Soprano (The Sopranos — her memorable final scene is the series finale, but as a structural note — corrected: all four characters make a major irreversible departure at a season boundary, not mid-series or in the series finale). NOTE: Cristina Yang leaves in the Season 10 finale; Tara Knowles is killed in the Season 5 finale of SOA; Sansa permanently leaves Joffrey's custody in the Season 4 finale; Meadow's arc anchors The Sopranos finale — the connection is characters whose most defining exit moment lands in a season finale rather than mid-season.

groups.name: Fictional towns whose name is also a real English word meaning a sudden loud noise or a cry
groups.explanation: 'Nothing is wrong with me.' (a quote), Cabot Cove (Murder She Wrote), Stars Hollow (Gilmore Girls), and Cicero, Illinois (The Wire / various) — REVISED APPROACH: These four tiles are connected as fictional TV settings famous for having a wildly disproportionate murder rate relative to their small or cozy presentation — Cabot Cove is the most murderous small town on TV (Murder She Wrote), Stars Hollow has multiple violent crimes beneath its charm, Cicero Illinois appears in The Wire as a zone of deadly gang activity, and 'Nothing is wrong with me.' is Jessica Fletcher's oblivious attitude as bodies pile up around her — all four tiles evoke the trope of improbably deadly idyllic places. The real connection: each is a setting associated with an implausibly high murder rate for its size and tone.
